doc.title: Phoebe Jacobs and Jackie Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 21, 2006

title: CD players and the 1937 Armstrong radio shows
summary: Harris names a Jordan CD; Jacobs describes finding 1937 Armstrong radio show discs now restored on CD.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: That’s great. When you get home, what’s on your CD player?
Now which home are you talking about? No I’m just teasing. Right now in my CD player is Stephanie and Marlon Jordan’s CD, a very good one. Do you have it?
Do you want to know what’s on my CD?

In 1937 Louis Armstrong was the first man of color to have a coast to coast radio show. A man by the name of Rudy Vallee was an ardent fan of Louis Armstrong’s and when his boss the Fleishman’s Yeast Hour, the president of the Fleishman Company asked him for a replacement, Rudy Vallee said I want Louis Armstrong to replace me for two months. And of course they wouldn’t hear of it. So he said, “Well I will break my contact or I want to hire Louis and I want to own the shows.” Those radio shows were done and they were all on matrix, those enormous metal discs. I discovered them in the house when I was clearing the house out when Mrs. Armstrong passed because Louis Armstrong and Lucille both left me in charge of the legacy and heritage. And I was taking care of all the papers and getting things ready for the college and giving some things to his sister, or whatever I was going to do I found these. And I gave them to a man in Washington because I had no equipment to play them, I didn’t know what it was. So they finally, it’s been I’d say 15 years they were working on this. We finally, they send me a CD and it’s in my house for me to listen to when I come back, of these radio shows.
1937. Isn’t that going to be something.
